status: Closed — governed commit status and resumable progress evidence verified on 2026-09-06
finding: Governed `atm git commit` can spend more than two minutes inside pre-commit without progress output, leaving the operator unable to tell whether it is hung or still validating after auto-stage succeeded.
expectedBehavior: Long-running governed commit hooks should emit phase heartbeats or a resumable receipt showing stage succeeded, hook is running, and the active branch-queue lock owner/pid.
evidenceOrRepro: The original timeout scenario is now covered by `node --strip-types tests/cli/git-commit-timeout-and-status.test.ts` (passed on 2026-09-06). The governed status route distinguishes no attempt, a live branch-queue owner with owner PID/aliveness, an in-flight or timed-out attempt, and a completed attempt with the actual commit SHA and post-attempt HEAD. This provides a safe resumable/status path without rerunning the commit blindly.
followUp: Keep `git-commit-timeout-and-status.test.ts` in the focused git-governance regression set. If a future report needs phase-level heartbeats beyond the existing status receipt, open a separate card with a fresh timing reproduction.
